title: Structured Programming
objectiveLead: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
bullets: Explain how pseudocode describes algorithms using plain language.
Identify common pseudocode keywords and control structures.
Use indentation to show hierarchy in pseudocode.

title: Pseudocode
paragraphs: Pseudocode: An informal way of describing an algorithm using plain language that resembles programming code but is not written in a specific programming language.
bodyBullets: Pseudocode should be written as plain language to allow you to simplify your thinking.
Pseudocode should be able to be translated to any programming language.
If your pseudocode looks the same as your Python code, then you are doing something wrong.

title: Pseudocode is Indented to Show Hierarchy
paragraphs: Just like in Python and many other programming languages, pseudocode uses indentation to help clarify what code is nested inside other blocks of code.
pseudocode:
START

    INPUT name

    message = "Hello" + name

    OUTPUT message

END

title: Sequence in Pseudocode
paragraphs: Follow the same sequence as the flowchart: receive a name, build a greeting, then display it.
pseudocode:
START
    INPUT name
    SET message TO "Hello" + name
    OUTPUT message
END

title: Selection in Pseudocode
paragraphs: Use the same temperature and threshold as the flowchart. Only the matching branch runs.
pseudocode:
START
    SET temp_celsius TO 25
    SET WARM TO 21
    IF temp_celsius > WARM
        OUTPUT "Wow, it sure is hot!"
    ELSE
        OUTPUT "Grab a sweater!"
    END IF
END

title: Iteration in Pseudocode
paragraphs: Repeat the same additions as the flowchart while i is less than 3, then display the total.
pseudocode:
START
    SET total TO 0
    SET i TO 0
    WHILE i < 3
        ADD i TO total
        INCREASE i BY 1
    END WHILE
    OUTPUT total
END

title: Wrap Up
bullets: Pseudocode describes an algorithm in plain language without relying on a particular programming language.
Use keywords to identify input, output, selection, iteration and functions.
Match control structures with their ending keywords so their boundaries are clear.
Indent nested steps to show the hierarchy of the algorithm.
